lines: My jokes have <wavy>loose threads</wavy>. Pull gently.
Woolwork jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with wool on them.
I keep a spare joke near the loom. It is not always ready for public use.
I told a joke at the loom once. The workstation took it better than the villagers did.
Shepherd jokes are woolly and hard to trim.
I had a sheep joke, but it wandered.
A loom joke needs good threads and better timing.
My blanket joke covers too much.
I told a wool joke and it got a little fuzzy.
A fence joke keeps the punchline in place.
The flock laughed once, but it may have been chewing.
I know a dye joke, but it changes depending on the shade.
A lamb joke is cute until it eats the setup.
My shears joke makes a clean cut.
The loom has a tight sense of humor.
I tried a counting joke and lost track halfway.
A blanket pun is warm, but not always welcome.
The sheep heard my joke and followed someone else.
I asked the ram for comedy advice. It butted in.
